name: Emily Loper
title: Senior Vice President of Public Policy, Transportation, Bay Area Council
background: Loper joined the Bay Area Council, a business-sponsored public-policy organization, in 2014 and leads its transportation policy work as Senior Vice President of Public Policy, Transportation. An East Bay native, she now lives in Oakland. She holds a Master of Public Administration from the USC Price School of Public Policy and a B.A. in Political Science and International Relations from UCLA, which recognized her with a Bruin Excellence in Civic Engagement award in 2023. Before joining the Bay Area Council, she worked in the legislative offices of U.S. Senator Dianne Feinstein and San Francisco Supervisor David Chiu. (Source: Bay Area Council staff bio page.)

At the Bay Area Council, Loper's transportation-policy work has included advocacy for Regional Measure 3, a $4.5 billion plan to fund Bay Area transportation projects approved by voters in 2018. For the November 2026 ballot, she is one of two named official proponents of record — alongside campaign organizer Lian Chang — for the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, the citizen initiative that qualified as Measure RTM: a 14-year, five-county regional sales tax projected to raise roughly $980 million a year for BART, Muni, Caltrain, AC Transit, VTA, SamTrans, and other regional transit operators. She and Chang, represented by the law firm Olson Remcho, filed the initiative's notice of intent to circulate on January 16, 2026. The Bay Area Council itself co-leads the broader Connect Bay Area campaign coalition alongside labor unions (SEIU Local 1021, ATU Local 1555), the South Bay Labor Council, SPUR, and other business and transit-advocacy groups. (Source: content/measures/scc-measure-rtm-2026.json in this voter guide; MTC's submission record for the initiative's circulation notice.)
